_comment: The graphs inside cat-harness's `openapi` subgraph, declared FROM WITHIN (#980): the `openapi` entry of `cat-harness.json` names this directory, and this node names what it holds. Each entry is `subgraph: true` — a directory of the INSTANCE (cat-harness), listed by `resolveDirectories` as if `cat-harness.json` had declared it, with `within: "openapi"`. These were the four directories of the `cat-openapi` instance until the owner folded it in, 2026-10-07: "put cat-openapi under cat-harness as named subgraph 'openapi', not separate repo." Ids were `cat-openapi-<dir>`; they are `openapi-<dir>` now, unique across cat-harness. Paths are relative to THIS directory.
name: openapi
_avatar_comment: The mark `cat-openapi.json` carried as an instance (bean sod4 #4), kept here because a directory entry has no `avatar` field in `ContentDirectorySchema` — a subgraph's mark is its tile's icon, and no `openapi` icon exists yet. Recorded so the glyph is not lost; nothing reads it.

_avatar.reads: braces — an API described as data

directories.description: The validators the openapi subgraph's code provides, one folio-validator/v1 node each naming the graph typology and $schema family it checks (bean riit). Owner, 2026-10-04: validators are KG nodes, and the validator names the family.

The graph typologies the openapi subgraph owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file (bean dmx1) — today one, `openapi`. Owner, 2026-10-04: no central registry for subgraph types; a harness declares its own in a typologies/ graph. Moved here from cat-harness/schemas/graph-typology-registry.ts, with each entry's code comments kept as its rationale.
The subgraph's shapes: `cat-openapi.config.json` (what an instance names), the ingest's provenance node, the subset of OpenAPI 3 the pages read, and how an operation's id is derived.

The rendering sub-pipeline: `ingest-openapi.ts` copies a configured document in verbatim with its provenance; `gen-openapi-pages.ts` writes a JSON-LD node and a thin page per document and per operation; `templates/` holds the one shared loader that draws them in the browser.
